## Morning Briefing — Tuesday, August 25, 2026

Today splits into two very different registers. The morning is developmental and low-stakes — Conscious Capitalism running 8 to 11 doesn't need prep and gives you three hours to think rather than perform. The afternoon flips hard: the AI Executive Workshop from 2 to 4 is a live client-facing deliverable with three open loose ends that need closing before you walk in, not during. And the day doesn't really end at 5 — SIM Enclave networking runs 11 PM to 2 AM, which means today is an 18-hour day bookended by a morning that asks nothing of you and a night that will cost you tomorrow's recovery. That's worth naming now, before it happens: the AI Workshop is the one piece of real leverage on the calendar today, and Aug 26 is already stacked with a client SAP meeting and 10+ meetings, so whatever gets deferred from tonight's late finish lands on an already-full day.

The execution reality is thinner than it should be. There's no task due today in OmniFocus, but that's a data quality problem, not a clean slate — the OmniFocus pull is over five weeks stale and 12 inbox items sit untriaged with 7 things overdue since May, June, and July, mostly health and Lifebook items you can't currently verify the status of. The thing most likely to slip today is the Derek Nwamadi thread: it's flagged high priority and needs a same-day answer on Friday SOW call availability (10a-12p or 1:30-4:30p), and it's sitting next to three other live threads — Systemic Compliance scheduling, MarketScale studio confirmation, and the UTB board meeting/voting request — that will all go stale if they wait past today. None of these are hard deadlines yet, but they're all one more day from becoming them. Separately, there's been no daily review logged since Aug 12. That's a two-week gap in a protocol that's supposed to run daily, and it means today's briefing is partially reconstructed rather than confirmed — worth restarting today rather than letting it compound into next week's heavy stretch.

The sharp edge today is the AI Executive Workshop itself. Prep docs are ready, but three specifics are still unconfirmed: whether Ayotunde's use-case catalog actually went out, whether the attendee list is locked, and whether Nicole Shanks' role in the room is clear. None of those are hard to close, but all three are exactly the kind of detail that turns a good workshop into an awkward one if they're still open at 1:45. Close them before lunch, not at 1:50. Layer onto that the Obsidian connector being down and OmniFocus data being unverified, and today's real risk isn't the workshop content, it's flying partially blind on commitments you can't currently audit. Treat the morning's open block as workshop-confirmation time, not free time, and use whatever's left to triage the OmniFocus inbox before it hits Wednesday.
